nodes.label: Progress checklist
nodes.rationale: A box is ticked only after its unit test passes, so the document cannot drift into optimism; structure-only tasks are ticked by hand and noted inline, and a parent stays unticked until every child is ticked.

nodes.label: D39 priority change — Hedera ATS is the primary deliverable
nodes.rationale: Every B1 qualification bar must be met because partial credit is worth nothing there; Track A is the credibility behind the submission, not the submission itself.

nodes.label: B1 Hedera ATS track
nodes.rationale: On-chain deployment is re-verified by a read-only suite against the public mirror node so a judge can run it without a key, and created_timestamp matching catches a swapped contract rather than only a missing one. The remaining gap is a funded Hedera account, so the API still resolves complianceGateway mock.

nodes.label: B2 HCS evidence anchoring + Merkle layer
nodes.rationale: Leaves prefixed 0x00 and nodes 0x01 so a node cannot pose as a leaf; odd nodes are promoted not duplicated, because duplication lets two leaf sets collide on one root; proof pairs are never sorted because position is what the proof claims. Anchoring counts as done only once a mirror node serves the root back.

nodes.label: B4 World ID Selfie Check integration
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (nullifier, action, signal) deliberately replaces the documented UNIQUE (nullifier, action), which would let each human approve exactly one payment ever. The nullifier is stored as Decimal(78,0) because field elements come back unpadded and text storage would make one person look like two. Signal binding is compared against hashSignal(expected) because the v4 verifier is never told which signal was expected, and our own clock is stored rather than upstream created_at.

nodes.label: B5 Chainlink CRE track
nodes.rationale: An earlier DEPLOYED-AND-ACTIVE claim was retracted: the gateway returned ACCEPTED while every execution failed in 0ms because confidential-workflows is a per-workflow entitlement not reported by cre whoami. Verdicts are now read off finished executions, never off the ACCEPTED response, and all four branches are proven because an always-MATCHED matcher would have looked identical on the happy path.

nodes.label: Track C — wiring the sponsor integrations into the flow
nodes.rationale: Three integrations were built and verified against real services yet none was load-bearing at runtime, which is a stated disqualifier; the goal of the track is that one payment cannot complete without passing through all of them.

nodes.label: PaymentHtlc.sol
nodes.rationale: No partial claims, no multi-hop, no cross-chain. Claim is restricted to the payee and closed once the timelock passes so claim and refund never overlap; refund is callable by anyone but funds only ever go to the recorded payer. The escrow itself is granted KYC, because the compliance gate applies to contracts too.

nodes.label: Row-level security on every public table (D46)
nodes.rationale: The database was wide open through Supabase's REST API — every table readable and UPDATE/DELETE permitted with only the publishable key, a key designed to ship in browsers. Re-asserted by a migration looping over pg_tables so a table added later cannot miss it.

nodes.label: VerifiableCredential model + lib/vc.ts
nodes.rationale: Credential body stays off-chain with the chain holding only a reference; expiresAt derives from aadhaarKycTtl and usable is computed on read, never cached, and an absent TTL becomes a far-future date rather than 0.

nodes.label: ComplianceGateway / AtsComplianceGateway
nodes.rationale: grantKyc carries a credential reference and no PII; Hedera ids resolve to EVM addresses via the mirror node rather than long-zero derivation, and a reverted grant is an error not a success. The read was verified to discriminate against a live bond, which is the only thing that makes it a control rather than a constant.

nodes.label: Open gap: nothing broadcasts a transfer
nodes.rationale: apps/approval-bridge/src/wallet-cli.ts stops at 'Local broadcast is not wired yet' — it signs nothing and sends nothing, so the recorded HTLC lock describes a movement something else must have made.

nodes.label: Open gap: the deployed CRE workflow predates D62
nodes.rationale: The DON runs plaintext name scoring against a minScore the config schema no longer has, while the lookup endpoint now returns only digests, so flipping VENDOR_MATCHER to cre would make every payment a mismatch. Source and deployment are separate artefacts and a passing test suite says nothing about which one the DON is running.
